data.name: Locomancer
data.detailed_description:
Play the game that started the trend! Accept no substitute!

Are you a kid that wants to play with model trains?

Are you an adult that misses playing with your model trains as a kid?

Are you an adult that missed out on playing with model trains as a kid?

Are you an adult with a kid that wants to play with model trains?

Are you just an adult that wants to play with model trains?

Are you a person of any age/race/gender that wants to play with model trains?

If you answered yes to any of the above, do I have news for you because Locomancer lets you PLAY WITH AND RIDE MODEL TRAINS!
(Also if you answered no to all of the above, come on, we all know you're lying to yourself and everyone you love. Take a break from the wave shooters and play with some trains.)

Locomancer is a toy box style model train simulator for touch enabled SteamVR headsets. It allows you to build layouts of varying complexity and even defy what is physically possible in fake virtual reality (reality).

Featuring:

  • Multiple locomotives including steam and diesel engines
  • A variety of rail cars including a fully functional cannon car
  • Straight track, curved track, inclined track, loop de loops, and more!
  • Various pieces of scenery to add detail your layouts

Plus, with support for custom scenery, you can bring models created by yourself or the community into the game for even further customization (Steam Workshop support coming soon). The possibilities are nearly endless*!

Fully embracing the physicality of touch enabled virtual reality you are legally required to build layouts piece by piece, tree by tree. Then, once complete you must remotely operate your trains with a replica DC control panel or hop in the cab of any of the available locomotives and drive them with physical levers, knobs, and dials! They even burst in to flames when they crash, you can't say that about your real model trains can you?

Oh...you can? I'd get that checked out if I were you.

So what are you waiting for? Become The Locomancer!

Yes, you are the Locomancer. Was that not clear? It's like a train wizard. You're like the babe with the power, but instead of voodoo it's train magic. Also, there's no magic dance, but you can still dance to twenty-six minutes of sweet big band jazz by Nathan Boler if you want to.

*The possibilities are totally endful, but there's still a lot you can do.

reviews.review:
Locomancer is a charming virtual reality sandbox that captures the fascination of model railways without requiring a spare room, an enormous collection of track pieces, or hours spent dealing with physical wiring. Developed and published by Eric Lipschutz, the game is built around constructing miniature railway layouts and then bringing them to life with controllable locomotives. Rather than relying on campaigns, strict objectives, or complicated management systems, it gives players a collection of railway components and encourages them to experiment. The result feels closer to owning an interactive virtual train set than operating a traditional railway simulator.

Building is the heart of the experience. Players can arrange track pieces to create simple circuits, sprawling routes, elevated sections, loops, and deliberately impractical constructions. The freedom provided by a virtual environment means there is little reason to remain completely realistic. A carefully organized miniature railway can be satisfying, but creating something ridiculous just to see whether a locomotive can survive the journey is equally entertaining. This flexibility gives Locomancer an approachable quality, especially for players who prefer open-ended creativity over completing predetermined missions.

The assortment of locomotives and rolling stock provides enough variety to make experimentation worthwhile. Steam and diesel engines help give different layouts their own character, while additional cars can be attached to create customized trains. Some equipment embraces the game's humorous side rather than attempting strict authenticity. The presence of unusual additions such as a cannon car demonstrates that Locomancer is comfortable being playful. Railway enthusiasts can certainly construct sensible layouts, but the game never discourages players from treating everything as a giant virtual toy box.

Scenery adds another important creative dimension. Tracks alone can quickly feel sterile, so environmental objects can be placed around the railway to turn an empty construction area into a miniature world. Arranging these objects complements the track-building process and makes each layout feel more personal. Custom scenery support further expands the concept by allowing players to incorporate additional models into their creations. This is particularly valuable for anyone who enjoys designing a setting as much as operating the trains themselves.

Virtual reality is central to how Locomancer works. Instead of controlling everything through conventional menus, players physically interact with many elements using tracked motion controllers. Railway construction consequently feels more like assembling an actual model set. Once a route is ready, trains can be controlled remotely through a recreation of a DC control panel, giving the player the familiar perspective of standing above a miniature railway and operating it from the outside.

An even more entertaining option is climbing aboard a locomotive and controlling it directly. Interactive knobs, levers, and dials provide a more tactile approach to driving, while the dramatic shift in scale changes how the railway is perceived. A layout that appears tiny while standing over it suddenly becomes a much larger environment when viewed from inside a train. Curves, inclines, scenery, and structures take on an entirely different character from this perspective. Riding through something that was personally assembled is arguably the game's most satisfying reward.

Physics prevent the sandbox from becoming too peaceful. Poorly designed tracks, excessive speeds, or reckless experimentation can produce crashes, and severe accidents can even leave locomotives burning. These consequences are more amusing than punishing and fit naturally with the game's experimental character. There is little pressure to protect a carefully managed transportation empire, so accidents often become part of the entertainment. The physics encourage players to test strange ideas simply to discover what happens.

The visual presentation is relatively simple, but that simplicity suits the miniature railway theme. Locomancer does not need photorealistic landscapes because its environments are intentionally reminiscent of constructed models. More important is the ability to clearly recognize, grab, position, and operate objects while wearing a VR headset. The accompanying big-band jazz music contributes considerably to the atmosphere, giving construction sessions a relaxed and slightly eccentric personality that complements the playful design.

Additional features strengthen the sandbox structure. Steam Workshop integration fits naturally with a game centered on customization, while achievements provide optional goals for players who want something beyond free-form construction. Steam Cloud support is useful for preserving progress, and online cooperative functionality allows the model railway concept to become a shared activity. Building or experimenting alongside another player can produce entertaining situations that would not necessarily emerge during solitary play.

The game's biggest weakness is also a consequence of its greatest strength: there is relatively little structure. Players looking for a detailed transportation economy, passenger scheduling, extensive progression, realistic railway operations, or a lengthy narrative campaign will not find those elements here. The player is expected to generate much of the entertainment through creativity and experimentation. Its presentation and mechanics can also feel modest compared with larger modern VR productions. Consequently, its long-term appeal depends heavily on how much enjoyment someone gets from repeatedly constructing and modifying railway layouts.

Steam Deck compatibility should be approached cautiously. Locomancer was fundamentally designed around SteamVR and tracked VR controllers rather than standard handheld controls. A Steam Deck alone does not provide the VR hardware or motion-control environment required for the intended experience, so it should not be considered a conventional Deck-friendly game. Players specifically seeking something they can install and comfortably play directly on the handheld should look elsewhere. Its natural home remains a PC-based VR setup with compatible equipment.

Ultimately, Locomancer succeeds as an imaginative virtual model railway rather than a serious train simulator. Its combination of hands-on construction, scenery placement, interactive train controls, changing perspectives, physics, customization, and playful experimentation gives it a distinctive personality. The experience is unquestionably niche, and its limited structure means it will appeal much more strongly to creative players than those seeking progression-driven gameplay. For VR owners who enjoy model trains, sandbox construction, or simply experimenting with miniature machines, however, it provides an entertaining way to build the railway layouts that physical space and practicality might otherwise make impossible.

Rating: 8/10
